analysis.summary: The PR introduces potential runtime crashes due to read-only object mutation and corrupts SEO/hreflang paths by incorrectly calculating AEM DAM identifiers.

bugs.title: Runtime crash due to mutation of frozen GraphQL response object
bugs.description: The helper function directly mutates the 'aemData' object (the result from an urql GraphQL query). GraphQL client response objects (like those from urql or Apollo) are typically frozen/read-only. Attempting to assign a value to 'featureAppTranslationsByPath' will throw a TypeError in strict mode.
bugs.risk: This will cause a complete runtime crash (TypeError) when attempting to load any page, as this helper is central to the page-model fetching logic.

bugs.title: Corruption of SEO/Hreflang paths causing broken language switching
bugs.description: The 'pathname' passed to the helper often already includes 'index' (e.g., from fetchAemNotFoundPageModel or fetchAemPageModel trailing-slash logic). The helper then calculates a 'hrefLangPageIdentifier' from this and appends 'index' again, resulting in invalid AEM paths like '.../indexindex' or '.../home/indexindex'.
bugs.risk: The 'pageList' returned by GraphQL will be empty because the filter paths are incorrect. This breaks SEO meta tags (hreflang) and the site's language/market switcher.

bugs.title: Duplicate population of hrefLangPathsFilter array
bugs.description: The 'hrefLangPathsFilter' array is populated in 'fetch-aem-page-model.ts' and then passed to 'getAemModelWithTranslationHelper'. The helper then executes the exact same loop, pushing duplicate filter expressions into the same array reference.
bugs.risk: Increases GraphQL query payload size unnecessarily and may lead to performance degradation or reaching query complexity limits on the AEM side.

notBugs.reason: Although 'item' can be null in AEM if no redirect exists, the existing code structure in fetch-aem-page-model.ts was not modified in this PR; only the data source was updated to the new helper, which maintains the same data shape.
